# Calzon's TTRPG Foundry — AI / Agent Discovery

Canonical site: https://mrcalzon02.github.io/HB-TTRPG-tools/
Capability manifest: https://mrcalzon02.github.io/HB-TTRPG-tools/api/foundry-capabilities.json
Operational argument contracts: https://mrcalzon02.github.io/HB-TTRPG-tools/api/operation-contracts.json
Resource collections: https://mrcalzon02.github.io/HB-TTRPG-tools/api/resource-collections.json
Browser facade: https://mrcalzon02.github.io/HB-TTRPG-tools/foundry-api.js
Human tool directory: https://mrcalzon02.github.io/HB-TTRPG-tools/site-map.html
Search index: https://mrcalzon02.github.io/HB-TTRPG-tools/search-index.json

## Integration doctrine

Mirrored calls, not mirrored logic. The site's existing generators, calculators, scientific laboratory engines, campaign data, rule JSON, and lore archives are authoritative. AI, MCP, plugin, and tool-calling adapters should discover and invoke those authorities rather than reproduce their algorithms.

GitHub Pages is a static origin. JSON/HTML resources are remotely retrievable with GET. Executable capabilities run through the canonical JavaScript modules (or an external MCP/tool bridge that mirrors their invocation descriptors). Do not infer a server-side RPC endpoint where none exists.

## Self-describing calls

Do not guess positional arguments or inspect implementation source as the normal integration path. `api/operation-contracts.json` is the public operational contract index. It documents capability call style, exact operation names, positional argument order, argument names/types/units/defaults/ranges/enums, nested public fields, return descriptions, context requirements, and examples where useful.

HBFoundryAPI exposes the same documentation programmatically:
- listOperationContracts()
- operationContract(capabilityId)
- operationContract(capabilityId, operation)
- describe(capabilityId) — includes the capability's operationContract inline
- listCapabilities(filter) — indicates whether a self-describing contract is available

Executable dispatch is contract-gated: a dispatch operation must both be allowed by the capability manifest and have a documented operational contract.

## Important callable engines

- spatial.module-map.generate — purpose-aware module/location generation.
- spatial.alien-vessel.generate — semantic multi-deck alien vessel generation.
- kaysender.airship.generate — Kaysender airship spatial generation.
- signals.configuration.analyze — full Signals Laboratory analysis.
- signals.utilities — RF, antenna, RLC, propagation, mapping, heterodyne, interfrequency, adaptive sampling, and experiment utilities.
- shadowrun.binary-cube — canonical Binary Cube Laboratory engine operations with individually documented arguments.
- blacklight.exo.jump.calculate — canonical EXO jump calculation when the EXO cartography page context is initialized.

Use the capability manifest for identity, runtime scripts, globals, invocation methods, status, and limitations. Use the operational argument contracts for constructing calls.

## Campaign, rules, and lore resources

The indexes register Kaysender wiki/index data; Blacklight character options, subgroup rules, factions, adversaries, equipment, artifacts, alien technology, character generator content, unified wiki, and Era campaign; the Warhammer 40K lore story archive; Barotrauma encounter/lethality packs; and the major Shadowrun, World of Darkness, Solanum Umbra, and module workspaces.

For in-browser or embedded-agent retrieval, HBFoundryAPI provides:
- listResources(filter)
- getResource(id)
- getPath(path, options)
- expandResourceIndex(id)
- searchResources(query, options)
- searchCollection(id, query, options)
- siteIndex({query})
- catalog(filter)

## Laboratories

The manifest treats laboratory capacity as a first-class surface. Portable solver engines (Signals Laboratory and Binary Cube) are callable and self-documented. Live Signals and other sensor/UI laboratories are separately identified as browser/device-context capabilities so external agents can discover them without falsely claiming headless access.

## Compatibility expectation

An external MCP/OpenAI-tool adapter should preserve stable capability ids, documented operation contracts, provenance/source paths, and the distinction between browser-js, browser-page-context, browser-ui, live-sensor, and static-resource modes.
